And they did not want to make king any of the brothers of al-Muntasir,
because they had all taken part in the plot to kill his father. Then the magnates brought al-Musta'in, the son of al-Mu'tasim, the brother of al-Ma'mun,
and they swore allegiance to him and made him king.
And in the year one thousand one hundred and eighty
[1180] of the Greeks,

to enter the territory of the Romans.
And the armies of the Romans met [them] at the Meadow of the Bishop {Marj al-Usquf} on the border of Melitene,
and they killed 'Umar and two thousand Arabs.
And when 'Ali the son of Yahya, the general, heard [this],
he likewise gathered a large army from Mayperqat and Armenia,
and went and met the Romans,
and he too was killed.
Now when the people of Baghdad and Samarra heard
that these two commanders were killed,
and that the Turkish slaves had gained dominion over the kingdom of the Arabs,
and whomever they wished they put to death,
and whomever they wished they kept alive and made king,
a multitude of the common people gathered together, and with them the market-folk and the vagabonds, and they went to the gate of the prison and broke it open,
and brought out the evil-doers,
and they all united.
And they cut the bridge over the Tigris,
and went into the treasury and plundered it,
and the registers of the scribes they burned with fire.
And they also plundered two courtyards of the Christians,
those of Bishr (or Bashshar?) and Abraham, the sons of Aaron.
Then the Turkish slaves mounted their horses,
and killed many of the vagabonds and others,
and the wrath subsided.
After al-Musta'in, al-Mu'tazz, the son of al-Mutawakkil, [ruled] four years and seven months.
In the year 251
[251] of the Arabs, when al-Musta'in went down from Samarra to Baghdad,
the Turks gathered together and brought out al-Mu'tazz and al-Mu'ayyad, the sons of al-Mutawakkil, from prison,
and they swore allegiance to al-Mu'tazz and made him king.
And they also swore allegiance to al-Mu'ayyad his brother, that he should reign after him.
And the people of Baghdad were with al-Musta'in,
while the people of Samarra were with al-Mu'tazz {text: al-Mutawakkil}.
And a great division fell among the Arabs,
and many were killed in the war that was waged between both sides.
And in the year
one thousand one hundred and seventy-four
[1174] of the Greeks, Michael, king of the Romans, died,
having reigned twenty-five years.
